title: Module 01: Environment Setup and First Planning Sheet

lab01-s000.title: Before You Start This Lab
lab01-s000.markdown:
**Estimated time:** 20 minutes
**What you will create:** A Plan item connected to Harborlight's semantic model and a Fabric SQL database, plus your first planning sheet. ---

lab01-s001.title: What You Will Do in This Module
lab01-s001.markdown:
Harborlight's actuals are in a managed semantic model, while planning remains disconnected from that model. In this module, you will connect the two. When you finish, you will have a planning interface that directly references FY25 actuals.

> [!WARNING]
> Actions can start or upgrade a billable session. According to the official documentation, a session for actions that qualify as **Planner** consumes **847 CU hours** and cannot be ended early. Distinguish the role displayed on the screen from actual billing, and review the actions, roles, and billing model in [Module 00](00-prerequisites.md) before proceeding.

---

lab01-s002.title: Step 1: Import the Semantic Model
lab01-s002.markdown:
1. Go to [app.fabric.microsoft.com](https://app.fabric.microsoft.com) and sign in.

   ![Microsoft Fabric sign-in landing screen, with the email address left blank](../assets/screenshots/lab01/01-fabric-sign-in-ja.png)

2. Open the workspace and folder specified by your instructor. If needed, select **New folder**, enter `Harborlight FY26 Plan`, and select **Create**.

   > [!NOTE]
   > If you were assigned an existing folder, use that folder instead of creating a new one.

3. Open the folder you created, or the specified existing folder, and select **Import** → **Report, Paginated Report or Workbook** → **From this computer**.

   ![Open the Import menu in the specified existing folder and display Report, Paginated Report or Workbook](../assets/screenshots/lab01/02-import-menu.png)

   ![Show From this computer in the report import submenu](../assets/screenshots/lab01/03-import-from-this-computer.png)
4. Select `Northwind_FMCG.pbix` and choose **Open**.

**Two items appear in the folder: a report and a semantic model.** Each has a role in this scenario.

![The imported Northwind_FMCG report and semantic model appear as two items in the specified folder](../assets/screenshots/lab01/04-imported-report-and-model.png)

lab01-s003.title: Before Continuing, Open the Report
lab01-s003.markdown:
Select the report and spend about a minute reviewing it. **At this stage, only view the report; do not modify the original.**

In the original scenario, this report represents the performance report Harborlight currently uses. However, the initial view of the PBIX imported for this exercise differs from the original description of “FY25 revenue by region, category, and quarter.”

![Initial view of the imported report: a matrix of administrative expenses, average selling price, and cost of goods sold, with region and city as rows and year as columns](../assets/screenshots/lab01/05-imported-report-default.png)

| Measure in the initial view | 2025 total (displayed value) |
|---|---:|
| Sum of Admin Expenses | 183,501.58 |
| Sum of Avg Selling Price | 14,119.56 |
| Sum of COGS | 2,020,234.86 |

This is an example of the sample PBIX's initial view. In Step 5, use `Plan Intro` to assign **2025 Gross Revenue** and reference the FY25 revenue baseline. The report's year column and the plan values you create in Plan are separate.

In this exercise, you will create an environment that distinguishes editable plan values from actuals while referencing the existing model.

The key point is that **you do not need to modify the existing report**. In the next seven modules, you will use the semantic model behind this report to create an FY26 plan. The report continues to work as before. In the standard SQL writeback used in this exercise, plan data is saved to a separate Fabric SQL database; the original semantic model is not changed automatically. See the note in [Module 04](04-forecast-and-writeback.md) for how to explicitly add the writeback table to a model.

There is no need to rebuild your established monthly reporting process for this exercise.

> [!NOTE]
> **In a real implementation, you do not need to import the sample.** You can connect the Plan item to the semantic model your organization already uses for reporting. Consider a configuration that references existing actuals and business metrics while allowing users to enter and adjust plan values.
>
> This exercise imports a `.pbix` to reproduce an “existing model” and make the exercise self-contained. The model does not have to be in the same workspace as the Plan item. In addition to view access to the workspace containing the model, the person connecting it needs both Read and Build permissions on the model. See [Module 00](00-prerequisites.md) for details.

> [!TIP]
> The translation source reports that you may see *"Refresh failed due to missing data source credentials."* The source says that its embedded sample data was visible and it was possible to connect to the planning sheet, but do not ignore the error unconditionally. **Before proceeding, confirm that the report displays the expected data and that the planning sheet can connect to the model and retrieve the required values.** If you cannot confirm this, investigate refresh history, data sources, credentials, and model settings with an administrator. See [Data notes](../data/README.md) for details.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Do not rename the semantic model connected to a Plan item. The [current official limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/overview-limitations) explain that renaming a connected model breaks the connection and prevents the Plan item from working with that model.

lab01-s004.title: Step 2: Create a Fabric SQL Database
lab01-s004.markdown:
You will use this database as the writeback destination for the forecast created in Module 04.

> [!NOTE]
> This SQL database is the writeback destination for Module 04; it is not a prerequisite for creating the Plan item.

1. Select **New item**, search for **SQL database**, and select it.
2. Add a distinctive name after `Northwind_FMCG_` (for example, `Northwind_FMCG_YourName`) and select **Create**.

   ![New SQL database dialog with a database name entered](../assets/screenshots/lab01/06-create-sql-dialog.png)

After it is created, confirm that the SQL database home page and Explorer are displayed.

![Home page of the created SQL database, displaying Explorer and Build your database](../assets/screenshots/lab01/07-created-sql-home.png)

> [!NOTE]
> This writeback destination is where plan data is output. Its purpose differs from the location where Plan app metadata is stored. Check [Module 00](00-prerequisites.md) and the workshop environment configuration to determine whether SQL or OneLake is used for metadata storage.

lab01-s005.title: Step 3: Create a Plan Item
lab01-s005.markdown:
1. Select **New item**, search for **Plan**, and select it.
2. Enter `Harborlight_FY26_Plan` in **Name**. Confirm that **Location** is the specified folder, then select **Create**.

   ![New Plan dialog with Harborlight_FY26_Plan and the specified folder entered](../assets/screenshots/lab01/08-create-plan-dialog.png)

Normally, the Planning landing page opens next. If it does not, reload the page and check access to the workspace and item. Seeing the saved item and being able to use the editing screen are different things.

![Plan, report, semantic model, SQL database, and related endpoints saved in the specified folder](../assets/screenshots/lab01/09-created-items-names-types.png)

> [!NOTE]
> The original describes a configuration in which a second SQL database is automatically created for Plan item metadata. The current [official FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/resources/frequently-asked-questions) also says that new Plan items store app metadata in OneLake. This serves a different purpose from the writeback database, so check the configuration in your workshop environment.

lab01-s006.title: Step 4: Create a Planning Sheet and Connect to the Semantic Model
lab01-s006.markdown:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Note about the connection method:** The original describes creating a shared cloud connection, but the current [official procedure](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-how-to-get-started) describes connecting directly with the signed-in user's ID. Check the screen in your workshop environment before following the steps below. If the screen does not require a shared cloud connection, you do not need to add a connection using the older method.

1. On the new Plan item's landing page, select **Planning**, or select **New Planning Sheet** on the **Home** ribbon. Name the planning sheet `Plan Intro` and select **Create**.

   ![New Planning Sheet dialog with Plan Intro entered](../assets/screenshots/lab01/12-plan-intro-create-dialog.png)

   ![Plan Intro created in Plan. The sheet appears in Explorer, with no fields assigned](../assets/screenshots/lab01/13-plan-intro-created.png)

2. In the planning sheet's **Data** pane, select **Add**. When **Select Semantic Model** opens, select **Semantic Model Item** and open the model selector.

   ![Select Semantic Model opened from Data with Semantic Model Item selected](../assets/screenshots/lab01/14-select-semantic-model.png)

3. Select the imported sample semantic model and choose **Add**. Check the model name on screen, and do not rename it after connecting.

   ![The sample semantic model displayed in the model selection screen](../assets/screenshots/lab01/15-model-picker-name.png)

   ![Select Semantic Model with Northwind_FMCG selected and Connect enabled](../assets/screenshots/lab01/16-selected-model-connect.png)

4. Select **Connect**. The connection uses the signed-in user's ID. The person connecting it needs both Read and Build permissions on the model.

   ![Semantic model added message and seven tables displayed in Data](../assets/screenshots/lab01/17-model-connected.png)

When the model's tables appear in the **Data** pane, assign fields in the next steps. If multiple models have the same name, use information such as the workspace or owner to choose the correct model. In environments where an ID is displayed, you can also verify the target `<semantic model ID>`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **You cannot change the connected model later.** A Plan item connects to only one semantic model throughout its lifetime. To create a plan from another source, you need a new Plan item.

lab01-s007.title: Step 5: Create Your First Planning Sheet
lab01-s007.markdown:
With the model connected, review the fields you will assign.

![Geography expanded in the Data pane, showing City, Region, and Sub Region. Rows, Columns, and Values have not been assigned yet](../assets/screenshots/lab01/18-data-geography-fields.png)

*In this sample model, **City, Region, and Sub Region** are under **Geography**. Select Region from Geography, and Category and Sub Category from Product.*

1. Open the `Plan Intro` sheet you created in Step 4. You do not need to create a duplicate sheet. If you connected to the model first in the older screen, create `Plan Intro` from **New Planning Sheet** on the **Home** ribbon.
2. Assign the following fields.

   | Field | Value to set | Source table |
   |---|---|---|
   | **Rows** | *Region* → *Category* → *Sub Category* | Region is in *Geography*; Category and Sub Category are in *Product* |
   | **Columns** | *Year*, *Quarter*, *Month Short* | *Date* |
   | **Values** | *2025 Gross Revenue* | *Measures Table* |

lab01-s008.title: Assign the Fields
lab01-s008.parent: Step 5: Create Your First Planning Sheet
lab01-s008.markdown:
Drag each of the following seven fields directly from **Data** to **Fields**, in order.

**① Geography's Region → Rows**

![Region assigned to Rows](../assets/screenshots/lab01/19-region-assigned.png)


**② Product's Category → second level of Rows**

![Category assigned below Region](../assets/screenshots/lab01/20-category-assigned.png)


**③ Product's Sub Category → third level of Rows**

![Region, Category, and Sub Category set as the three Rows fields](../assets/screenshots/lab01/21-rows-assigned.png)


**④ Date's Year → Columns**

![Year assigned to Columns](../assets/screenshots/lab01/22-year-assigned.png)


**⑤ Date's Quarter → second level of Columns**

![Quarter assigned below Year](../assets/screenshots/lab01/23-quarter-assigned.png)


**⑥ Date's Month Short → third level of Columns**

![Year, Quarter, and Month Short set as the three Columns fields](../assets/screenshots/lab01/24-columns-assigned.png)


**⑦ Measures Table's 2025 Gross Revenue → Values**

![Measures Table expanded, just before selecting the revenue measure limited to 2025](../assets/screenshots/lab01/25-select-revenue-measure.png)


![After assigning all seven fields, the All row for 2025 Gross Revenue shows 25.87, with the unit in Millions](../assets/screenshots/lab01/26-fy25-baseline-millions.png)


> [!NOTE]
> FY25 revenue in the sample PBIX is **25,866,900.40**. Displayed in millions with two decimal places, it is **25.87**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Measures Table contains both **Gross Revenue** and **2025 Gross Revenue**, but they behave differently. *Gross Revenue* covers all years in the model, so the sheet displays columns from 2023 through 2026. *2025 Gross Revenue* is filtered to FY25 and displays only that year's baseline for this exercise: **US$25.87 million ($25.87M)**. **COGS** and **2025 COGS** follow the same pattern.
>
> Select *2025 Gross Revenue* here. Selecting a measure that is not limited to a year does not produce an error, but it creates a multi-year sheet whose numbers will not match those in Module 02.

> [!TIP]
> The **Data** pane groups dimensions and measures by their tables. Expand **Semantic Model** to see seven tables: *Measures Table*, *Date*, *Fact Transactions*, *Geography*, *P&L Measures*, *P&L Rows*, and *Product*. If you cannot find *Region*, expand **Geography**, not the fact table. See [`data/README.md`](../data/README.md) for details about each table.

This sheet is the foundation for the remaining exercises. Expanding it to quarters / months and configuring collaboration will be covered in later steps.

lab01-s009.title: Save the Sheet
lab01-s009.parent: Step 5: Create Your First Planning Sheet
lab01-s009.markdown:
Select **Save** in the upper-right corner and wait for **Saving...** to disappear.

![Plan Intro saved. All is 25.87 in Millions, and the role badge is Planner](../assets/screenshots/lab01/27-save-result.png)

lab01-s010.title: Step 6: Connect to the SQL Database
lab01-s010.markdown:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Procedure for environments that require a shared SQL connection:** The current [official FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/resources/frequently-asked-questions) deprecates the shared database connection and says new Plan items store app metadata in OneLake. The [official database connection procedure](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-how-to-create-database-connection), on the other hand, describes this connection as optional. **Do not conclude that a connection is required just because a banner is displayed.** Check the target Plan's storage method and the actual sharing / collaboration path you will use, and follow these steps only if this connection is needed. Do not add a connection if the screen has no such setting. Configure the writeback destination in Module 04.

1. Select **Set up connection** in the upper-right corner.

   ![Select Fabric SQL Connection, describing a connection that enables collaboration in Reading View for workspace Viewers](../assets/screenshots/lab01/32-viewer-collaboration-connection.png)


2. In **Select Fabric SQL Connection**, select **Create Connection**. In the connection editor, select **Create new connection** and set the authentication type to **Organizational account**.

   ![Organizational account selected as the authentication type in connection credential settings](../assets/screenshots/lab01/33-collaboration-connection-settings.png)

3. Enter a connection name and select **Create**. The original example is `Northwind_FMCG`. Follow the naming conventions of your workshop environment, if any.

4. Select the connection you created and choose **Connect**. If the connection does not appear in the list, reload the page and check the connection status and permissions. Consult the administrator before creating a duplicate connection.

---

lab01-s011.title: Step 7: Review the Screen Layout
lab01-s011.markdown:
Reviewing the screen layout now will make later operations easier. The displayed tabs may vary depending on the mode and environment.

| Display mode | Tabs and actions at the top of the screen |
|---|---|
| **Reading** | Home, Planning, Model, Format, Writeback, and others |
| **Editing** | May include additional tabs and actions such as Infobridge |

The following describes **Editing** mode. Each ribbon tab is primarily used for the following tasks.

| Ribbon tab | Main actions |
|---|---|
| **Home** | Create planning sheets, PowerTables, and Intelligence sheets |
| **Planning** | Layout, formatting, inserting rows / columns, bulk editing, filtering, and auditing |
| **Model** | Forecasts, scenarios, driver-based models, cubes, and approvals |
| **Format** | Conditional formatting and semantic formatting |
| **Writeback** | Writeback destination, settings, and logs |
| **Infobridge** | Data integration and linking plans across sheets |

lab01-s012.title: Expand the Planning Ribbon First
lab01-s012.markdown:
Select the **Planning** tab. In compact view, some commands and group names are omitted. Notes and other commands are under **More options**, so expanding the ribbon makes them easier to find in later exercises.

![Compact view of the Planning ribbon, with commands in one row and group names omitted](../assets/screenshots/lab01/39-compact-planning-ribbon.png)


Select the **Full View** button at the right edge of the ribbon to expand the entire ribbon.

![Planning ribbon expanded with Full View, showing group names, Totals, Number, Notes, and other items](../assets/screenshots/lab01/40-full-planning-ribbon.png)


The expanded **Planning** ribbon has groups such as the following.

| Group | Actions displayed |
|---|---|
| **Layout & Number** | Layout, Totals, Quick format, percentage, currency, and decimal places |
| **Rows & Columns** | Insert Row, Manage Rows, Formula, Number, Simulate, Text, Checkbox, Person, List, Date, Manage measures, Show Columns |
| **Tools** | Bulk Edit, Pivot, Top n, Filter, Optimize, Filter context |
| **Actions** | Audit, Notes, Writeback, Reset, Export |
| **Default** | Undo |

Whether an action is enabled depends on the selected cell and the state of the sheet.

lab01-s013.title: Find Notes and Comments
lab01-s013.markdown:
**Notes** is in the **Actions** group on the Planning ribbon. **Comments** is not on that ribbon; it is in the upper-right corner on the same row as the tab names. Notes are fixed annotations, while Comments is a separate feature for managing conversations and comment lists.

Open the **Comments** dropdown in the header. It may show the following items:

- **Add Comment**
- **View All Comments**
- **Settings**

![Comments menu in the header, showing Add Comment, View All Comments, and Settings](../assets/screenshots/lab01/41-comments-menu.png)

lab01-s014.title: Review the Panes and Footer
lab01-s014.markdown:
- **Upper-right, beside the ribbon tabs:** In Editing mode, Security, Comments, Editing, Save, and other items are displayed.
- **Left:** The **Explorer** pane. Use it to add, manage, and switch sheets.
- **Right:** Panes and icons such as Data, Fields, Filter, Comments, Bookmarks, and **Parameters**. The display name corresponding to the original's “formula pane” is **Parameters**. Use **Data** for model tables and **Fields** to arrange rows, columns, and values.
- **Footer:** Information such as the number of rows and columns and page position is displayed. Sum, Avg, and Count for the selected range may also appear.
- **Gear icon in the lower-right:** Use **Settings** to configure items such as the number of rows per page.

---

lab01-s015.title: Reload the Saved Sheet and Verify It
lab01-s015.markdown:
After saving, reload the page and confirm that you can display the same Plan and sheet.

![Reading mode after reloading the page. Plan Intro, year 2025, All 25.87 in Millions, and the Planner badge are retained](../assets/screenshots/lab01/28-reloaded-plan-intro.png)


The Fields pane is not displayed in Reading mode. Switch back to Editing to verify the saved layout as well.

1. Open the **Reading** dropdown in the upper-right and select **Editing**.

   ![Editing can be selected in the Reading dropdown](../assets/screenshots/lab01/29-mode-selector.png)

2. If **Confirm Action** displays **Do you want to retain properties in edit mode?**, select **Save and Proceed** to continue.

   ![Confirmation when switching to Editing mode. Select Save and Proceed to continue](../assets/screenshots/lab01/30-retain-edit-properties.png)

3. After returning to Editing, verify the layout in the Fields pane.

   ![Returned to Editing after reload, confirming that three Rows, three Columns, and one Value field were retained](../assets/screenshots/lab01/31-reloaded-editing-fields.png)

lab01-s016.title: What You Have Accomplished
lab01-s016.markdown: You now have a planning environment connected to Harborlight's reporting model. A writeback database is also available, and FY25 actuals are displayed on screen. You have not entered any plan values yet. In the next module, you will allocate the board's US$30 million revenue target based on the prior year's mix.

lab01-s017.title: Knowledge Check
lab01-s017.markdown:
1. Why are you advised not to rename the semantic model or workspace?
2. You discover that you need to plan from a different semantic model partway through the quarter. What should you do?
3. In the original SQL configuration, there are two SQL databases in the workspace. What is each one for? What should you check if the current configuration differs?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Current official limitations explain that renaming a model connected to a Plan item breaks the connection, and renaming a workspace containing a Plan item prevents the item from opening.
2. Create a new Plan item. You cannot change the model connected to an existing item.
3. One is the writeback destination for plan data that you created. In the original configuration, the other is automatically created to store Plan item metadata. The current FAQ also describes storage in OneLake, so verify the actual storage method and created items.

</details>

---
